the role of retinoids in breast cancer progression.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RA treatment of breast cancer cells induces expression of COUP-TF II and VE-cadherins, and that the COUP-TF I I and TGFβ receptor kinase are required for the formation of cell networks.

RA treatment of breast cancer cells results in a complex set of molecular and morphological changes that can be divided into two major categories: (1) a subset of genes are induced that have endothelial cell genotypic elements, and (2) the cells undergo morphological changes that include the formation of networks and cell fusion.
RA induces a subset of breast tumor cells to undergo endothelial transdifferentiation and that the TGFβ receptor kinase is a critical mediator of the endothelial transdifferential process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RA induces a subset of breast epithelial cancer cells to undergo a transdifferentiation process into cells with endothelial characteristics.
RA can promote endothelial transdifferentiation and network formation by two distinct mechanisms, one involving induction of COUP-TF II and the other induction of VE-caderin.
